newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa gets set to host Zaire talks - source.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa gets set to host Zaire talks - source.

text.p: A government source confirmed on Friday that South Africa had been asked to host peace talks between Zairean rebels and representatives of President Mobutu Sese Seko early next week.
The source told Reuters that senior foreign ministry officials had started laying the groundwork for negotiations, which were likely to take place on Monday or Tuesday.
"Senior foreign ministry officials began preparations on Friday to host peace talks in South Africa early next week."
He added that as yet no location had been decided, but Cape Town and Gauteng have been fingered as sites.
Earlier on Friday Zairean rebels said talks would take place in South Africa on Monday or Tuesday.

"If nothing changes then the talks will be in South Africa and will begin on either Monday or Tuesday," Moise Nyarugabo, secretary-general at rebel headquarters, told Reuters in the eastern city of Goma.

Another South African government source declined to confirm the country would host peace talks. He added that South Africa's role was to act "merely as a facilitator" with all announcements coming from the concerned parties themselves.

Nyarugabo said the essential issue for the talks would be to negotiate the transfer of power from Mobutu to a transitional government led by the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) led by Laurent Kabila.
The rebels have seized about a quarter of Africa's third largest country and insist that a ceasefire in the six month civil war can only be declared after negotiations have begun.
